discovery: Aberration-corrected electron optics enabling sub-ångström transmission electron microscopy

nominees.name: Harald Rose
nominees.affiliation: Technische Universität Darmstadt and Universität Ulm, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / electron optics
motivation: For decades, Scherzer's theorem held that round electron lenses have unavoidable spherical aberration, limiting the resolution of electron microscopes far above the electron wavelength. Harald Rose designed a hexapole corrector that could overcome this limit. In 1997–98, Maximilian Haider and Knut Urban built it and demonstrated it in a working transmission electron microscope. This turned a theoretical design into a practical instrument. Aberration correction now gives sub-ångström resolution, the direct imaging of single atoms and light elements, and atomic-resolution spectroscopy. These capabilities underpin modern materials physics: precipitates in alloys, interfaces in oxides and semiconductors, defects in batteries, catalysts and two-dimensional materials. Correctors are now standard in laboratories worldwide. They have changed how we connect atomic structure to macroscopic properties. This invention in physical instrumentation has had broad, lasting impact across physics, chemistry and engineering.
